newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Poland ready to reschedule grain swap - Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Poland ready to reschedule grain swap - Bulgaria.

text.p: Bulgaria's agriculture ministry said on Thursday Poland was prepared to reschedule the return of 100,000 tonnes of wheat due by November 30 and had suggested that the Balkan country could repay the grain in cash.
Poland supplied Bulgaria with 100,000 tonnes of wheat to ease a shortage in March, against exports from the new crop.

Deputy Agriculture Minister Bogdan Kenderov told Reuters that during his visit to Warsaw last week Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz had suggested that Bulgaria could pay for the wheat in cash rather than grain.
"At our meeting the Polish Prime Minister told us that Bulgaria might pay in cash for the grain if it finds wheat prices on the Polish bourse acceptable," Kanderov said.

At a separate meeting Polish Agricultural Minister and Deputy Premier Jaroslaw Kalinowski said his country was willing to help Bulgaria in its economic crisis and suggested the payment could be rescheduled.
Kanderov said Bulgaria's agriculture ministry would invite Kalinowski to visit later this month to negotiate the exact terms of the payment.
Under the current terms of the contract, Bulgaria must return 100,000 tonnes of wheat to Poland between October 1 and November 30 in exchange for grain imported in March.
Also, under two commercial contracts agreed with Swiss firm Glencore in March and May, Bulgaria must return a further 131,750 tonnes by November 1 in exchange for 100,000 tonnes imported.

The ministry had forecast a wheat harvest of 2.4 million tonnes this year, up from last year's 1.8 million, but officials said that due to adverse weather the harvest, which started last week, might be lower.
Bulgaria suffered acute grain shortages earlier this year following uncontrolled wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996.
The cabinet imposed last week a 15 percent grain export tax until year-end in a move to offset further grain imports.
